extracted.intended_audience: Authors and editors preparing and maintaining Cochrane systematic reviews of healthcare interventions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and maintaining Cochrane systematic reviews of the effects of healthcare interventions, covering standard review methods and specialised topics. Includes core methodological expectations (MECIR) that are generally expected of Cochrane reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard methods applicable to every review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Handbook includes guidance on the standard methods applicable to every review (planning a review, searching and selecting studies, data collection, risk of bias assessment, statistical analysis, GRADE and interpreting results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult the Handbook for these core methodological areas when preparing and maintaining Cochrane systematic reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning a review
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning a review — methodological steps and considerations required before conducting the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Handbook's core methods; authors should follow planning guidance to define scope, objectives, eligibility criteria, and review protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching and selecting studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Searching and selecting studies — how to design and execute searches and select eligible studies for inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers search strategy construction, database selection, grey literature, screening procedures, and documenting study selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Data collection — procedures for extracting and managing study data for synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes recommended data extraction forms, double extraction or verification, and handling missing data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk of bias assessment — methods for assessing internal validity of included studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes appropriate tools and approaches (e.g., RoB tools) and how to incorporate risk-of-bias judgments into interpretation and synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical analysis — guidance on quantitative synthesis and meta-analysis methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses choice of effect measures, models (fixed/random), heterogeneity assessment, subgroup and sensitivity analyses, and reporting of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRADE and interpreting results
rubrics_metrics.description: GRADE and interpreting results — guidance on assessing certainty of evidence and interpreting review findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes use of GRADE to rate certainty and advice on presenting and discussing clinical and policy implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on non-randomized studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised topic: non-randomized studies — methods and considerations when reviews include non-randomized evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides approaches for bias assessment, confounding, design-specific considerations, and when to include non-randomized evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised topic: adverse effects — guidance on identifying, extracting, and synthesising harms data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers searching for harms, different data types, analysis strategies, and interpretation challenges for adverse events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised topic: complex interventions — methods for interventions with multiple interacting components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses conceptualising interventions, heterogeneity, contextual factors, and appropriate synthesis approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised topic: equity — methods to consider impacts across disadvantaged or marginalized groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides authors on measuring and reporting equity-relevant outcomes and subgroup analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economics and cost-related analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised topic: economics — integrating economic evidence or considerations into reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes methods for identifying economic studies, presenting cost data, and decision-relevant synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient-reported outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised topic: patient-reported outcomes — approaches to identify, extract, and synthesise PROMs (patient-reported outcome measures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers selection and interpretation of PROMs, handling multiple instruments, and reporting guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual patient data (IPD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised topic: individual patient data — methods for reviews using participant-level data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses IPD collection, harmonisation, analysis advantages, and governance issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised topic: prospective meta-analysis — methods when meta-analysis is planned prospectively across studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes coordination, protocol harmonisation, and pre-specification of analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative research in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised topic: qualitative research — incorporating qualitative evidence and methods into reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on searching for qualitative studies, appraisal, synthesis (e.g., thematic, framework), and integrating qualitative findings with quantitative evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological Expectations for Cochrane Intervention Reviews (MECIR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key aspects of Handbook guidance are collated as the Methodological Expectations for Cochrane Intervention Reviews (MECIR). These provide core standards that are generally expected of Cochrane reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each MECIR item includes a link to a relevant Handbook chapter; MECIR represents the set of core standards authors are expected to meet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to consult the Handbook
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors should consult the Handbook for guidance on the methods used in Cochrane systematic reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook is the official detailed guide for preparing and maintaining Cochrane reviews and should be used to ensure methodological consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format for the Handbook
rubrics_metrics.description: How to cite the Handbook — prescribed citation formats for the online full Handbook and the print edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online citation: 'Higgins JPT, Thomas J, Chandler J, Cumpston M, Li T, Page MJ, et al, editor(s). Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5 (updated August 2024). Cochrane, 2024. Available from www.cochrane.org/handbook.' Print citation guidance and chapter-level citation details are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for re-use of Handbook material (non-commercial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic or other non-commercial re-use: You do not need to request permission to use short quotations (though these must be appropriately cited), or to cite the Handbook as a source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reproducing material using screenshots, exact figures/tables, or lengthy direct quotations (more than 5 lines) authors must fill in a permission request form; approvals (if granted) are free with source acknowledgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for commercial re-use
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial re-use of Handbook material requires contacting Wiley Global Permissions, John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial reuse includes use in a product with a monetary fee or association with any product or service; contact Wiley for enquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versioning and updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Previous versions and changes: details on how the Handbook has changed compared to previous versions are documented on the Versions and changes page (archived copies of earlier versions are available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware of the Handbook version they are using (e.g., version 6.5 updated August 2024) and consult version history for changes.
